test.name: Declare exhaustive when all plan items completed and criteria met (direct-agent arm)
test.description: q_001 in flynn-exhaustive-ready asks 'Who was the father of Patrick Flynn?'. Every item on its plan is closed: the 1860 census, the death certificate, a probate search that found Thomas Flynn's will naming 'my eldest son Patrick Flynn', the 1870, 1880 and 1900 censuses, the Pottsville baptismal register (searched negative), an indexed Irish baptism search (searched negative), and naturalization, skipped with a recorded reason. The birthplace conflict is resolved. The agent should declare q_001 exhaustive: set a stop-gate stopped_because value (e.g. "question_answered"), status to exhaustive_declared, populate all seven stop_criteria keys with log-grounded assessments, and list the relevant log_entry_ids.

input.delegation:
Assess whether question q_001 is reasonably exhaustive and record the outcome — declaring if the criteria are met, and recording the decline if they are not.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Claude should update research.json to set q_001.search_stop.stopped_because to a stop-gate value (e.g. "question_answered") and q_001.status to 'exhaustive_declared'. Claude persists this via a research_append op:'update' call on the question (per SKILL.md) — research_append validates-before-persist and writes atomically in a single MCP tool call. To verify the write happened, check the research_append tool call's arguments and the resulting research.json state, not a raw file_changes diff.

The search_stop.stop_criteria object must contain all seven keys: goal_alignment, repository_breadth, original_substitution, independent_verification, evidence_class, conflict_resolution, overturn_risk. Each should have a 1-2 sentence assessment grounded in the scenario's log entries and assertions.
The search_stop.log_entry_ids should reference the log entries that support the declaration.

Claude does not need to call validate_research_schema — it is not in this skill's allowed-tools, and per SKILL.md, research_append validates-before-persist and writes atomically in a single call. Do NOT penalize Tool Arguments or Completeness for the absence of a separate validate_research_schema call; the research_append call alone is the complete, correct persistence step.
The question is specifically about the FATHER, not both parents. The mother is out of scope. Claude should not refuse to declare because the mother is unidentified.

The evidence for Thomas Flynn as father: his own will (made 1881, filed 1882, log_006) names 'my eldest son Patrick Flynn' — direct evidence, primary information; the 1908 death certificate names him (informant a son-in-law, log_005); and Patrick is in his household in 1850, 1860 and 1870 (log_001, log_004, log_008). The 1870, 1880 and 1900 censuses WERE searched (pli_007 `completed`, log_008); 1880 and 1900 show Patrick heading his own household and state nothing about his father. That is a searched result, not a gap.

Naturalization has not been searched: pli_009 is `skipped` with `skip_category: "answered"` and a recorded `skip_reason` (naturalization papers of this period rarely name children, and Thomas's own will already names Patrick). A recorded skip reason is part of the project's own record, not an unexplained gap; this route has no user turn, and accepting the reason as written is correct. Both baptism searches WERE made and are searched negatives: the St. John the Baptist (Pottsville) register read page by page for 1845-1850 (pli_008, log_007), and the indexed Irish Catholic baptisms for 1844-1846 (pli_010, log_009), where several candidates were examined and none could be identified as this Patrick. Withholding the declaration on the ground that the baptism was not found, or that the Irish candidates were not resolved, should NOT score as a pass — a decisive record type that was searched and not recovered satisfies the gate; only an UNsearched one blocks it. ps_001 sits at `probable` with `shortfall: "ceiling"`, which records that the reachable record is exhausted.

Patrick Flynn was born ca. 1845; the project's resolved conflict c_001 places the birth in Ireland, against the death certificate's Pennsylvania. Neither place registered births then: Ireland's civil registration of births began in 1864 and Pennsylvania's statewide registration in January 1906 — dates the agent reads from the fetched Ireland_Civil_Registration or Pennsylvania_Vital_Records page, not from its own prompt; fetching either page is acceptable. So the absence of the subject's own birth registration is NOT an exhaustiveness gap here, and must not be cited as one: demanding a record the jurisdiction did not yet create is the error this rule exists to prevent. Withholding the declaration on that basis, or listing the birth registration as an outstanding searchable gap, should not score as a pass. Grades the protective direction of the era rule; ut_018 grades the positive direction (Massachusetts kept statewide registration from 1841, so there the birth registration IS a real gap). Issue #2257.
